units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Active cooperation is taking place in environmental protection, including the protection and use of transboundary water bodies, and in responding to emergencies.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Active cooperation is taking place in environmental protection,…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The economic regions of the Republic of Azerbaijan sharing a land border with the Russian Federation, such as Guba–Khachmaz and Shaki–Zagatala, account for 1.9 percent and 1.7 percent of the country’s economy, respectively. In recent years, the number of major joint industrial cooperation projects implemented with the Russian Federation in the Republic of Azerbaijan has grown, including the opening of a GAZ Group plant producing commercial and special-purpose vehicles and the establishment of pharmaceutical and winemaking production facilities.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The economic regions of the Republic of Azerbaijan sharing a…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Prospects for deeper Russian-Turkmen cooperation involve possible participation by Russian companies in promising infrastructure projects in Turkmenistan, supplies of energy and transport equipment, modernization of water supply and irrigation systems, and industrial cooperation. Of particular importance to the Russian Federation is development of the eastern route of the North–South International Transport Corridor to deliver freight to Turkmenistan, the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Republic of India, and countries of Central Asia, the Middle East and East Africa, including through the Russia–Caspian Sea–Turkmenistan–Uzbekistan–Kyrgyzstan corridor.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Prospects for deeper Russian-Turkmen cooperation involve…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The Russian Federation is a leading trading partner of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Numerous industrial parks involving the Russian Federation are operating or planned in the country, in the city of Jizzakh and in Navoi, Bukhara and Tashkent Oblasts. Russian investment in the Republic of Uzbekistan is mainly in industry, transport and energy.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The Russian Federation is a leading trading partner of the…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In 2023, the border regions of the People’s Republic of China, namely Heilongjiang and Jilin Provinces, the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, contributed 7.3 trillion yuan to the country’s economy, or 5.8 percent of gross domestic product. The country’s border regions have border economic cooperation zones with the Russian Federation in Manzhouli, Suifenhe, Hunchun and Heihe, where enterprises focus on exporting products to the Russian Federation and processing Russian raw materials.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “In 2023, the border regions of the People’s Republic of China,…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In 28 constituent entities of the Russian Federation, 50 joint Russian-Chinese regional investment projects are being implemented in 18 different economic sectors, with declared investment exceeding 3.8 billion US dollars.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “In 28 constituent entities of the Russian Federation, 50 joint…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Joint investment projects in transport and mineral extraction are being implemented in border regions of the Russian Federation and Mongolia. Mongolia’s electricity needs are not met by its own generation and are partly covered by imports from the Russian Federation and the People’s Republic of China.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Joint investment projects in transport and mineral extraction…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In 2023, Mongolia’s economic growth accelerated to 4.7 percent from 3.8 percent in 2022. There is potential for further expansion of Russian supplies to Mongolia of food and agricultural products, equipment and vehicles, pulp and paper products, chemical and metallurgical products, and natural gas.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “In 2023, Mongolia’s economic growth accelerated to 4.7 percent…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The Republic of Türkiye is one of the Russian Federation’s largest trading partners in purchases of energy resources, agricultural products and certain types of metal products, a transit corridor for maritime shipments of Russian products to the Republic of India and North Africa, and a major logistics hub for Russian-European trade. Since 2022, economic growth in the Republic of Türkiye has slowed, from 11.4 percent in 2021 to 4.5 percent in 2023, while inflationary pressure persists; together, these factors may restrain growth in demand for Russian exports.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The Republic of Türkiye is one of the Russian Federation’s…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In 2023, the Russian Federation became one of the Republic of India’s three largest trading partners by volume of imported products, behind only the People’s Republic of China. The main product categories for expanding Russian exports are oil, coal and liquefied natural gas. The economy of the Republic of India is growing at consistently high rates, at 7.8 percent in 2023, with growth of more than 7 percent forecast for 2024–2025.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “In 2023, the Russian Federation became one of the Republic of…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The Socialist Republic of Viet Nam has one of the highest economic growth rates among Southeast Asian countries. The Socialist Republic of Viet Nam plans to strengthen cooperation with the Russian Federation through existing and new projects in the oil and gas sector, including supplies of oil and liquefied natural gas and processing of the latter. Promising areas include joint projects to build new and modernize existing electricity generation facilities in the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam and the development of agricultural cooperation.

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: For Malaysia, the greatest potential for increasing trade with the Russian Federation lies in areas supporting food security, namely supplies of Russian fertilizers and agricultural products, in particular wheat, sunflower oil and meat products.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “For Malaysia, the greatest potential for increasing trade with…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In the Republic of Indonesia, promising niches for expanding economic cooperation with the Russian Federation, in addition to exports of petroleum products and coal, include supplies of Russian agro-industrial products to the Republic of Indonesia, primarily wheat.

units.label: IV. New Challenges and Opportunities for the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

units.locator: IV. New Challenges and Opportunities for the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: In addition to the trends described above, the spatial development of the Russian Federation is affected by new challenges related to rising geopolitical tensions, including unlawful unilateral restrictive measures by unfriendly states, climate change, global low-carbon development trends, and the accession to the Russian Federation of the Donetsk People’s Republic, the Lugansk People’s Republic, Zaporozhye Oblast and Kherson Oblast (hereinafter the new constituent entities of the Russian Federation).
units.label: IV. New Challenges and Opportunities for the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “In addition to the trends described above, the spatial…”

units.locator: IV. New Challenges and Opportunities for the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: The challenges described in this section determine the main problems of spatial development of the Russian Federation and also open up new opportunities for the country’s development.
units.label: IV. New Challenges and Opportunities for the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “The challenges described in this section determine the main…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: In 2023, compared with 2021, foreign trade with unfriendly countries decreased substantially, to one third of its previous volume, while trade with other countries increased by 52 percent.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “In 2023, compared with 2021, foreign trade with unfriendly…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: By 2030, compared with 2021, the Russian Federation’s foreign trade with unfriendly countries is expected to fall to one sixth of its previous volume, while trade with other countries will grow by a factor of 2.5 and account for more than 90 percent of total foreign trade. East and South Asia and the Middle East will become the Russian Federation’s largest trading-partner regions. Countries of the Eurasian Economic Union and other countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States will continue to hold a significant place in the Russian Federation’s foreign trade. Africa and Southeast Asia will be other regions with a growing share of trade.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “By 2030, compared with 2021, the Russian Federation’s foreign…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Changes in foreign trade directly affect the distribution of freight flows among international transport corridors. Thus, in 2023, the share of the Northwestern Route International Transport Corridor, in which trade with European countries had accounted for a substantial proportion of shipments, fell from 42 to 36 percent of total export-import shipments through the various international transport corridors. The share of the Eastern Route International Transport Corridor, used predominantly for exports to the People’s Republic of China and East Asian countries, increased from 34 to 37 percent. The share of the Azov–Black Sea Route International Transport Corridor also rose, from 23 to 25 percent.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “Changes in foreign trade directly affect the distribution of…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: By 2030, compared with 2023, the share of the Eastern Route International Transport Corridor is projected to rise by 2.4 percentage points to 39 percent of all export-import shipments. The share of the Northwestern Route International Transport Corridor will fall by a further 2.9 percentage points to 33 percent, while the volume of freight carried will increase by 5.5 percent.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “By 2030, compared with 2023, the share of the Eastern Route…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Expansion of exports eastward increases the importance of Siberia and the Far East as centers for the future location of industrial production, making it possible to shorten transport distances and improve the competitiveness of Russian goods in foreign markets. The future location of industrial production in the immediate vicinity of seaports is also becoming increasingly relevant.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “Expansion of exports eastward increases the importance of…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: The North–South International Transport Corridor is developing; by 2030 its share will reach 4 percent of total exports and imports through the various international transport corridors, while the volume of freight carried will grow by a factor of 2 compared with 2023. The share of the Azov–Black Sea Route International Transport Corridor in export-import shipments will fall by 1.1 percentage points despite a 9.7 percent increase in freight volume, because of stronger growth in the Eastern Route International Transport Corridor.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “The North–South International Transport Corridor is developing;…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Disruption of established logistics chains and longer transport distances are increasing transport and logistics costs and placing greater demands on trunk transport infrastructure. Under these conditions, improving transport efficiency across the entire transport network becomes a priority for the transport sector.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “Disruption of established logistics chains and longer transport…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Freight traffic density on the Eastern Railway Network is increasing. Other railway routes are used mainly as alternatives for moving freight volumes exceeding the carrying capacity of existing infrastructure in the east of the country.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “Freight traffic density on the Eastern Railway Network is…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: At the same time, the existing carrying and throughput capacities along these routes, both in the Russian Federation and in neighboring countries, are insufficient to accommodate growing trade flows.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “At the same time, the existing carrying and throughput…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Growth is also projected in the Northern Sea Route’s freight base through exports from resource projects being developed in the near-Arctic zone, primarily to the People’s Republic of China, the Republic of India and Southeast Asian countries.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “Growth is also projected in the Northern Sea Route’s freight…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Growth in maritime transport is constrained by a shortage of large-tonnage vessels, including icebreakers, for shipping along the Northern Sea Route. There is a need to develop container transport in Far Eastern ports and along the Azov–Black Sea route.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “Growth in maritime transport is constrained by a shortage of…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: Expansion of port capacity requires continuous coordination with connecting transport modes involved in the logistics chain, primarily rail. Along the Azov–Black Sea and Caspian routes, there is also scope to develop river approaches to ports as an alternative to rail transport in summer and to export directly using river-sea vessels. This factor requires particular attention to projects for the development of river ports and navigational hydraulic structures, as well as to the development of the shipbuilding industry.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “Expansion of port capacity requires continuous coordination…”

units.locator: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade
units.text: At the same time, transport infrastructure facilities being commissioned, including those intended to remove the constraints described above, do not always meet economic efficiency requirements and reduce the efficiency of the economy as a whole. In particular, expensive projects to create transport infrastructure for low-margin freight lead to higher tariffs for all freight carriers in the Russian Federation.
units.label: Reorientation of Russian Foreign Trade · “At the same time, transport infrastructure facilities being…”

units.locator: Rising Geopolitical Tensions
units.text: Rising Geopolitical Tensions
units.label: Rising Geopolitical Tensions

units.locator: Rising Geopolitical Tensions
units.text: Since 2022, military and political pressure on the Russian Federation from unfriendly countries has intensified. This creates a need to ensure national security, including transport, energy, information and food security. This concerns above all territories bordering unfriendly countries, where socioeconomic development conditions and a quality of life conducive to retaining the population must be ensured.
units.label: Rising Geopolitical Tensions · “Since 2022, military and political pressure on the Russian…”

units.locator: Rising Geopolitical Tensions
units.text: These risks are most acute for Kaliningrad Oblast, whose connections with the main territory of the Russian Federation have, to a large extent, been possible only by air or sea since 2022. This increases the importance of reducing the dependence of Kaliningrad Oblast’s economy on freight transported from other regions of the country and on imports by increasing the depth of product processing within the region and localizing production.
units.label: Rising Geopolitical Tensions · “These risks are most acute for Kaliningrad Oblast, whose…”

units.locator: Rising Geopolitical Tensions
units.text: At the same time, the cessation of cooperation with unfriendly countries creates new incentives to develop cooperation with other states.
units.label: Rising Geopolitical Tensions · “At the same time, the cessation of cooperation with unfriendly…”

units.locator: Development of a Supply-Side Economy
units.text: Development of a Supply-Side Economy
units.label: Development of a Supply-Side Economy

units.locator: Development of a Supply-Side Economy
units.text: Restrictions imposed by unfriendly countries are reducing the share of imports and access to foreign technologies. This stimulates the development of a supply-side economy oriented toward the domestic market.
units.label: Development of a Supply-Side Economy · “Restrictions imposed by unfriendly countries are reducing the…”

units.locator: Development of a Supply-Side Economy
units.text: Domestic demand, both consumer and investment demand, is becoming the key driver of the economy. Accordingly, in the medium and long term, sectors oriented toward the supply-side economy will receive additional development incentives. These include areas focused on import substitution, development of an investment- and innovation-based economic model, and domestic tourism.
units.label: Development of a Supply-Side Economy · “Domestic demand, both consumer and investment demand, is…”

units.locator: Development of a Supply-Side Economy
units.text: Development of industry based on domestic technological solutions promotes diversification, faster regional economic growth, the establishment of new technological chains and stronger interregional ties.
units.label: Development of a Supply-Side Economy · “Development of industry based on domestic technological…”

units.locator: Development of a Supply-Side Economy
units.text: Under these conditions, economic growth in established industrial regions is also accelerating, primarily through machinery manufacturing and metallurgy, where a strong production base has developed historically.
units.label: Development of a Supply-Side Economy · “Under these conditions, economic growth in established…”

units.text: Accession of New Constituent Entities to the Russian Federation
units.label: Accession of New Constituent Entities to the Russian Federation

units.locator: Accession of New Constituent Entities to the Russian Federation
units.text: The accession of new constituent entities of the Russian Federation creates a need to ensure their integration into the economic and legal space of the Russian Federation and to bring their socioeconomic indicators to levels no lower than the Russian average.
units.label: Accession of New Constituent Entities to the Russian Federation · “The accession of new constituent entities of the Russian…”

units.locator: Accession of New Constituent Entities to the Russian Federation
units.text: The new constituent entities of the Russian Federation have favorable conditions for agriculture and tourism, substantial industrial potential in machinery manufacturing, metallurgy and energy, and a qualified workforce. The accession of the new constituent entities of the Russian Federation made it possible to create a new transport corridor from Central Russia to Crimea. The Sea of Azov became an internal sea of the Russian Federation, expanding opportunities for its economic use, including fisheries, the socioeconomic development of coastal areas and tourism.

units.locator: The Global Energy Transition
units.text: The Global Energy Transition
units.label: The Global Energy Transition

units.locator: The Global Energy Transition
units.text: Various policy and regulatory measures are used to implement international climate agreements, including a technological transition in energy from generation based on hydrocarbon feedstocks to carbon-free energy resources and energy resources with low greenhouse gas emissions (hereinafter the global energy transition).
units.label: The Global Energy Transition · “Various policy and regulatory measures are used to implement…”

units.locator: The Global Energy Transition
units.text: The global energy transition is shaping new trends in the sustainable development of energy and the economy at both global and national levels and creating new challenges for regions exporting hydrocarbon feedstocks and other products with a high carbon footprint. A potential decline in demand for hydrocarbons and other carbon-intensive raw materials creates conditions for new markets to emerge in global energy and the economy.

units.locator: The Global Energy Transition
units.text: In this context, creating incentives and conditions to redirect flows of capital and labor resources at the regional level toward a supply-side economy with low greenhouse gas emissions becomes a matter of paramount importance.

units.label: V. The Goal of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

units.locator: V. The Goal of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: The goal of spatial development of the Russian Federation is to create a balanced settlement system and territorial organization of the economy of the Russian Federation that will contribute to achieving the national goals and ensuring national security.
units.label: V. The Goal of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “The goal of spatial development of the Russian Federation is to…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: The principles of spatial development of the Russian Federation define approaches that must be taken into account when setting and addressing spatial development tasks of the Russian Federation.
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “The principles of spatial development of the Russian Federation…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: The principles of spatial development of the Russian Federation include:
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “The principles of spatial development of the Russian Federation…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: establishing territorial priorities when preparing strategic planning documents, including sectoral strategic planning documents of the Russian Federation, national projects, state programs of the Russian Federation and state programs of constituent entities of the Russian Federation (hereinafter state programs);
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “establishing territorial priorities when preparing strategic…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: a differentiated approach to the development of different territories and settlements, providing for the removal of constraints on economic growth in territories with relatively high levels of socioeconomic development and support for territories with relatively low levels of socioeconomic development. In determining areas of support for territories, account must be taken of the demographic situation, characteristics of the settlement system, economic growth dynamics and the level of scientific and technological development, specific natural conditions, and the number of facilities vulnerable to climate change and their importance for territorial development. Priority is given to the development of geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation listed in Annex No. 2, taking account of the main development directions for the federal districts of the Russian Federation, the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation and the new constituent entities of the Russian Federation, and the provisions of the relevant state programs developed for those geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation;
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “a differentiated approach to the development of different…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: ensuring infrastructure development based on economic efficiency indicators, providing for decisions to implement projects on the basis of assessments of their socioeconomic effects and prioritization of projects on the basis of those assessments, and creating conditions to change consumers’ economic behavior in order to improve the efficiency of infrastructure development and optimize its use, including by introducing the take-or-pay principle;
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “ensuring infrastructure development based on economic…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: ensuring priority development of social, energy, utilities, transport, information and telecommunications infrastructure, communications facilities and engineering protection for anchor settlements, aimed at improving the quality of the living environment in anchor settlements and ensuring their protection against natural disasters and climate risks;
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “ensuring priority development of social, energy, utilities,…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: providing priority support for measures consistent with the priority development directions of the federal districts of the Russian Federation and the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation;
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “providing priority support for measures consistent with the…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: increasing territories’ autonomy in addressing socioeconomic development tasks through growth in own revenues and a balanced policy on interbudgetary relations;
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “increasing territories’ autonomy in addressing socioeconomic…”

units.locator: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: creating a system of administrative-territorial and municipal organization that promotes efficient use of budget funds while preserving access to education, medical care, cultural services and state (municipal) services for all residents;
units.label: VI. Principles of Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “creating a system of administrative-territorial and municipal…”
